newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index drops 2.0 pct at provisional close.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index drops 2.0 pct at provisional close.

text.p: Share prices lost on Thursday nearly one-third of their previous day's gain at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) as the rebound drew more sellers with no news to push the market, brokers said.
The 30-share BSE index ended 58.80 points, or 2.0 percent, at a provisional 2,882.56, off 2,878.20 low, after rising 5.1 percent on Wednesday.
"We continue to believe that the bear phase has not yet run its full course," said broking firm ING Barings in a note. "It is a good opportunity to restructure portfolios."
Traders said Wednesday's rally was propelled by misconceptions of an economic revival and government incentives in the first quarter of 1997.
"(Such) hopes will be belied as fundamentals continue to deteriorate," ING Barings said.
Analysts said the players had doubts on the government's ability to offer sops to revive sagging markets and boost slowing industrial output.
"The near-term scenario is pretty grim," said Sunil Kothari at broker Nagindas Kothari. "There's distinct possibility of petrol (and other fuels) prices being raised very soon."
Cement production and despatches in November were higher than in October, latest industry figures showed but cement stocks were hit by sellers.
ACC fell 39.50 rupees to 1,000 and Gujarat Ambuja Cement shed 6.50 to 221.50.
ING Barings told investors to sell cement and auto stocks.
TELCO dropped 10 rupees to 318, M&M 4.0 to 311 and Bajaj Auto 0.50 to 723.
SBI lost 7.50 rupees to 209, Reliance 7.25 to 187.50 and TISCO 6.75 to 153.75.
